description:
## Why

PKIX-ng0x decomposition, child 4 of 5. After successful validation,
callers need to read the attributes out. RFC 5755 §4.2.7 defines the
`attributes` SEQUENCE.

## What

1. Public API:
   - `AttributeCertificate::attributes()` returning an iterator over
     `Attribute<'_>` where `Attribute` exposes:
     - `oid()` returning `ObjectIdentifier`
     - `values()` returning an iterator of `der::AnyRef`
2. Standard attribute helpers for the common types defined in
   RFC 5755 §4.4 (Role, ChargingIdentity, Group, Clearance, etc.):
   - Each gets a typed accessor like `iter_roles()` returning an
     iterator of `&Role` so callers do not hand-parse the AnyRef values.
3. Crucially: attribute extraction is ONLY exposed via a
   `ValidatedAttributeCertificate` newtype. The raw
   `AttributeCertificate::parse_der` result does NOT expose attributes,
   only validation outcome does. This prevents callers from reading
   attributes off an unvalidated AC.

## Tests

- [ ] Round-trip: parse, validate, iter_attributes returns the same
      AttributeTypes as encoded.
- [ ] Three standard attributes from §4.4 (Role + Group + Clearance)
      have typed accessors that match openssl-decoded values.
- [ ] Attempting to read attributes from a raw (unvalidated)
      AttributeCertificate is a compile error.

## Depends on

PKIX-ng0x.3 (validation must exist; only validated ACs expose
attributes).
title: pkix-ac: attribute extraction public API
